channel.title: TrendingTesla
channel.description: The Tesla ecosystem and the AI race, explained.

item.title: SpaceX relaunched from one pad after 32 hours
item.description: SpaceX flew two Falcon 9 rockets from SLC-4E at Vandenberg 32 hours, 3 minutes and 21 seconds apart, its fastest turnaround from one pad. NROL-136 lifted off on 22 November 2026 after USSF-317 on 20 November.

item.title: Neuralink enrolled 21 people in its trials
item.description: On 28 January 2026 Neuralink said 21 people were enrolled in its trials worldwide. Reuters reported the same figure the same day. The company also said it had no serious device-related adverse events.

item.title: Tesla taped out the AI5 chip design
item.description: On 15 April 2026 Elon Musk said Tesla's team had taped out the AI5 chip. Electrek and TechNode both reported the post. Tape-out sends a finished design to be manufactured.

item.title: Tesla shut down the Dojo training computer
item.description: In August 2025 Bloomberg reported that Tesla was disbanding the Dojo team. Musk then said Dojo 2 was an evolutionary dead end and that the work would focus on AI5 and AI6.

item.title: A household socket supplies about 1300 watts
item.description: Tesla's Gen 2 Mobile Connector manual rates the ordinary household adapter at 1.3 kW on a 120-volt socket. Electrek reported the same 1.3 kW ceiling.

item.title: New Teslas lost the included mobile charger
item.description: Tesla stopped including the Mobile Connector with new orders after 17 April 2022 and sold the cable separately. Musk cited low use.

item.title: Tesla's wall charger also fits other cars
item.description: Tesla's Universal Wall Connector charges NACS cars and, with a built-in J1772 adapter, other electric cars. Its top output is 11.5 kW.

item.title: Tesla started Semi deliveries in Nevada
item.description: On 24 September 2026 Tesla handed Semi trucks to customers from its factory in Sparks, Nevada. It still did not publish a price or a delivery count.

item.title: Neuralink participant plays GTA VI with his mind
item.description: On 20 November 2026 Neuralink posted a video of about two minutes in which a clinical-trial participant plays GTA VI with his brain implant, one day after the game’s worldwide release. The implants remain investigational and are not approved by the FDA or other regulators.

item.title: HSBC more than doubles its Tesla price target
item.description: On 20 November 2026 HSBC analyst Michael Tyndall upgraded Tesla to Hold from Reduce and raised the price target to $359 from $157, about 129 percent higher, on a possible SpaceX combination. The new target is still below Tesla's close of $374.41 on 19 November.

item.title: Tesla starts rolling out FSD v15 to testers
item.description: On 21 November 2026 Tesla said on X that FSD (Supervised) v15 is starting to roll out, first to Early Access Program members in software update 2026.38.6.11. Tesla claims 25 times better handling of safety-critical cases, a figure that is not independently verified, and the driver still has to pay attention.

item.title: Himes threatens SpaceX funding over Ukraine Starshield slowdowns
item.description: On 20 November 2026 Jim Himes asked Elon Musk to explain October Starshield slowdowns in Ukraine, and wrote that supporting funding for SpaceX-developed government systems is difficult until those answers arrive. No funding restriction has been imposed.

item.title: Nvidia fell 14 percent after Anthropic's debut
item.description: On 20 November 2026, one day after Anthropic's record listing, Nvidia lost about 14 percent and the Nasdaq 5.3 percent. Anthropic, Tesla and SpaceX all fell too.

item.title: Italy approves Tesla Assisted Driving before the EU
item.description: Italy's transport ministry gave provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the European name for FSD (Supervised), on 20 November 2026. Italy is the 12th European country to allow it and the first large EU market.

item.title: Investors funded 44 billion dollars of SpaceX chips
item.description: Apollo and Goldman Sachs priced about 44 billion dollars of notes on 20 November 2026 to buy Nvidia Vera Rubin chips that SpaceX will lease. It is the largest GPU financing so far, and the chips arrive in the first half of 2027.

item.title: Tesla now sells cars in Argentina
item.description: Tesla launched in Argentina on 20 November 2026 with the Model 3 and Model Y, sold online from 41,590 dollars. The first showroom is in a shopping centre north of Buenos Aires, and the first cars reach buyers in March or April 2027.

item.title: Anthropic made the biggest stock debut ever
item.description: Anthropic sold shares at 83 dollars and started trading on Nasdaq as ANT on 19 November 2026. With the extra shares the banks bought, the listing raised about 93.5 billion dollars, more than any IPO before it.

item.title: Tesla wants to make solar silicon in Texas
item.description: Tesla has applied for a Texas school-tax break for a 3.1 billion dollar plant that would make solar-grade polysilicon from 2030. The application says Tesla would not build it in Texas without the break.

item.title: SpaceX Caught Starship After 22 Hours
item.description: On Flight 15, SpaceX caught the Starship ship 22 hours and 32 minutes after liftoff. The booster's catch was aborted over the Gulf. The 22-hour figure is SpaceX's own timeline.

item.title: DeepSeek opens its chat tools
item.description: DeepSeek said on 13 November 2026 that a full set of application APIs is available on deepseek-flash, and that a demo chat client is open source.

item.title: Meta releases small model Muse Ember
item.description: Meta released Muse Ember on 9 November 2026 and called it the smallest and most efficient model for tool calls, short coding tasks, routing and extraction.

item.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max
item.description: Alibaba Cloud unveiled Qwen4-Max in Hangzhou on 16 November 2026. The company says it has 2.4 trillion parameters and a 1 million token context.

item.title: Anthropic starts its stock roadshow
item.description: Anthropic said on 10 November 2026 that it has started the roadshow for a listing. The expected price range is 70 to 78 dollars a share.

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on 9 November 2026. They are the same underlying model, with different access rules.

item.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon
item.description: Google said on 10 November 2026 that Gemini 4 Carbon is available to developers, companies, scientists and consumers.

item.title: Starlink's new satellites are raising their orbits
item.description: All 26 Starlink V3 satellites launched on Starship Flight 15 are healthy and have started climbing toward their working orbits, Starlink engineering lead Michael Nicolls said on 14 November 2026.

item.title: Grok Bot 1.0 now joins whole teams
item.description: SpaceXSI launched Grok Bot 1.0 on 11 November 2026. Shared bots can enter Slack, Microsoft Teams and video calls, and the company says they can offer to take on work.

item.title: Boring expects Nashville riders in early 2027
item.description: In a 17 November 2026 interview, Boring Company CEO Steve Davis said he expects the first mile of the Music City Loop to carry passengers in the first quarter of 2027. That is his bet, not an opening date.

item.title: Neuralink opens a US trial after stroke
item.description: Neuralink’s PRIME2 study, posted on ClinicalTrials.gov on 10 November 2026, is recruiting adults with spinal cord injury, ALS, or chronic ischemic stroke. The registry lists no implants and no results yet.

item.title: United now flies Starlink on most flights
item.description: United said on 12 November 2026 that Starlink Wi-Fi is on more than half of its daily flights, with nearly 64 percent expected by the end of 2026. The service is free for MileagePlus members.
